newsitem.title: ITALY: Pirelli rises in Milan, analysts bullish.
newsitem.headline: Pirelli rises in Milan, analysts bullish.

text.p: Italian tyre and cable group Pirelli ended 0.54 percent up at 2,817 lire, one of the few gainers on a lower Milan bourse on Friday after a meeting with analysts appeared to have paid off, traders said.
"We are pleased about the fact the company has set itself goals and is achieving them," said Elisabetta Villa, analyst at Milan brokers ASV, who attended Thursday's presentation.

Another factor cited by those present was Pirelli's aim to raise its profitability margin in the cables sector to 10 percent, announced by group managing director Marco Tronchetti Provera who said he was also confident of winning new contracts abroad in the short term.

Another interesting prospect was the company's participation in a Malaysian dam project in which Pirelli hoped to be awarded a stake which would mean expendiure of $1.6 billion for cables and accessories.
Pirelli last week announced a near doubling of first half profits as its tyre business rebounded back to health and its cables operations continued to thrive and grow.
It said first half 1996 consolidated net profits rose to 206 billion lire from 115 billion despite half-year overall sales falling some 3.5 percent to 5.37 trillion lire.

Pirelli said it expected better results for 1996 compared with 1995 when the group showed net consolidated profits of 304 billion lire, a result which itself doubled from 1994 on annual sales up 11 percent.
"Given the first half trend it's clear that Pirelli's reorganisation strategy is paying off, that can be seen clearly at the level of margins growth." said Lucio Cannamela, analyst at Pasfin.
In the cables sector, the profitability margin was 8.4 percent in the first half 1996 against 7.2 percent in the second half of 1995 and 6.1 percent in the first half of 1995.
No similar forecasts had been made for the tyres sector.

The group's automotive tyre interests grouped under Amsterdam-listed Pirelli-Tyre, 81-percent owned by Pirelli SpA, showed a first half profits leap while it also looked forward to further improvements in the second half of 1996.

For the whole group, "the closure of Armstrong (tyre company) in the U.S., already announced to the press, will result in a reduction in extraordinary charges from 1997," said Cannamela. The tyre business should also benefit in the second half this year from a trend of falling rubber prices, he added.
